subject: science
name: Science
title: Grade 10 Science: Chemistry
overview: Grade 10 Science provides collegiate-level scientific inquiry across chemical, physical, and environmental systems aligned with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS).
competencies: Design empirical laboratory investigations, analyze complex data sets, and account for experimental error.
Model atomic, molecular, physical, and ecological systems using mathematical and conceptual tools.
Apply scientific principles to solve technological and ecological problems through engineering design.
Evaluate the ethical, societal, and environmental consequences of scientific discoveries.

modules.title: Atomic Structure, the Periodic Table & Chemical Bonding
modules.description: Investigating electron configurations, periodic trends, ionic and covalent bonding, and molecular geometry.

topics.title: Subatomic Particles and Quantum Electron Orbitals
topics.description: Modeling protons, neutrons, electrons, energy levels, and orbital configurations (s, p, d, f).

topics.title: Periodic Trends: Electronegativity, Ionization Energy & Radius
topics.description: Using the periodic table to predict relative atomic size, ionization energy, and chemical reactivity.

topics.title: Chemical Bonding: Ionic, Covalent and Metallic Structures
topics.description: Modeling Lewis dot structures, polar vs. nonpolar bonds, and VSEPR molecular geometry.

modules.title: Chemical Reactions, Stoichiometry & the Mole Concept
modules.description: Balancing chemical equations, applying Avogadro's number, calculating molar mass, stoichiometry, and limiting reactants.

topics.title: Classifying and Balancing Chemical Reactions
topics.description: Balancing synthesis, decomposition, single replacement, double replacement, and combustion reactions.

topics.title: The Mole Concept and Stoichiometric Calculations
topics.description: Converting between grams, moles, and liters of gas at STP, and determining theoretical yield.

modules.title: Thermochemistry, Kinetics & Chemical Equilibrium
modules.description: Measuring enthalpy changes (delta H), activation energy, reaction rates, catalysts, and Le Chatelier's principle in reversible reactions.

topics.title: Endothermic vs. Exothermic Reactions and Calorimetry
topics.description: Calculating heat transfer using q = mc(delta T) and interpreting potential energy diagrams.

topics.title: Collision Theory, Reaction Rates and Chemical Equilibrium
topics.description: Applying Le Chatelier's principle to predict shifts in dynamic equilibrium when temperature, pressure, or concentration change.
